title: TypeScript SDK: resumable stream protocol + edge/runtime adapters
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Customers using long-lived streaming responses (chat sessions, stepwise generation) hit two classes of pain: 1) transient network failures or page refreshes cause client-side consumer state to be lost, and 2) runtimes like Deno/Edge Workers and older browsers expose different stream primitives and backpressure semantics. Existing internal playbooks assume a full re-connect or a simple 'resume from last token' which produces duplicated tokens, missing partial frames, or dangling consumers.

Goal: Design and implement a small, runtime-agnostic "resumable stream protocol" plus lightweight TS SDK shims for major edge/browser/Deno streaming primitives. The protocol should: a) allow checkpointing at safe framing boundaries, b) encode minimal recovery state clients can present on reconnect, c) propagate cancellation and consumer swap semantics across adapter boundaries, and d) remain backwards-compatible with existing streaming endpoints (no breaking server change required).

Design summary:
- Checkpoint frames: introduce optional zero-byte-delimited JSON checkpoint frames that the server can emit between logical tokens. These frames contain stable prefixes (sequence id, byte offset, epoch) that the SDK uses to resume. The SDK will not require the server to change: it will also support client-driven checkpointing using token counts or encoded KV cache references.
- Framing rules: adopt a deterministic framing boundary based on UTF-8 codepoint completion for text and explicit frame-length prefix for binary payloads. The SDK adapters will be responsible for detecting partial multi-byte sequences and only emit checkpoints at safe boundaries.
- Resume API: SDK exposes reconnect(options: { resume_token?: string, prefer_delta?: boolean }) where resume_token is an opaque string produced by the client from last checkpoint. On reconnect the SDK will attempt to align the stream; if server sends preface indicating it cannot resume, SDK will fall back to idempotent re-issue with de-dup heuristics.
- Dual-consumer handoff: provide a lightweight 'handoff()' helper in the TS SDK to allow safe transfer of a stream from one consumer to another (useful for hot reloads, tab-to-tab transfer). Handoff will coordinate abort signals and ensure no token duplication via the checkpoint token.
- Runtime adapters: implement three adapters in the SDK: Node ReadableStream/AsyncIterable adapter, Web Streams API adapter, and Deno/Edge-specific adapter that normalizes limited backpressure and different cancel() behaviors. Each adapter maintains the same external async iterator contract and exposes a common small runtime hint API for diagnostics (e.g., lastCheckpoint, pendingBytes).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We avoid changing server contract by making checkpoint frames optional and by favoring client-side heuristics when servers are unavailable. This adds complexity to the SDK but preserves compatibility.
- Checkpoint frames add a tiny wire overhead when used; we'll gate emitting them behind a sampling config and an explicit enable flag per request.
- Perfectly deduplicating tokens across all models and prompts is impossible without model-side hooks; the SDK will provide best-effort heuristics (prefix match + sequence ids). We'll document residual duplication risk for ultra-low-latency apps.

API examples (TypeScript):
- Basic resumable connect:
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-llama-3', enableCheckpoints: true });
for await (const chunk of stream) { render(chunk.text); /* SDK saves checkpoint after each safe boundary */ }

- Reconnect with resume token:
const { resumeToken } = await client.chat.getLastCheckpoint();
const resumeStream = client.chat.stream({ resume: resumeToken });

- Handoff helper usage:
const stream = client.chat.stream();
const newConsumer = await handoff(stream, { migrateAbortSignal: true });
await newConsumer.consume();

Test plan:
- Unit tests for framing detection: multi-byte UTF-8 sequences, binary length-prefix parsing, partial boundary detection.
- Integration tests across runtimes: Node 18+, Deno 1.32+, Chromium-based browsers and WebKit nightlies. Use playwright to simulate tab reloads and network blips.
- Chaos tests: synthetic network pauses while streaming to assert checkpoint alignment and no token duplication beyond 2 tokens 99th percentile.
- Backpressure simulation: create a slow consumer and verify adapters do not explode memory and that the Node/Deno adapters map cancel signals correctly.

Docs and rollout:
- Draft PRD + protocol doc in Drive: link below.
- Soft-launch behind SDK flag enableResumableStreams; telemetry to track resume success rate and duplicate-token incidents.
- After 2 weeks and telemetry targets met, flip the default to enabled for hosted SDKs.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype framing detector and unit tests (week 1).
2) Implement Node/Web/Deno adapters and small API surface (week 2).
3) Integrations + chaos + telemetry hooks (week 3).
4) Docs, examples, and polyfills for older browsers (week 4).

acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes reconnect/resume API and handoff helper with TypeScript definitions and JSDoc
Adapters for Node / Web Streams / Deno exist and pass the adapter compatibility matrix
Unit and integration tests for framing and resume behavior in CI
Telemetry events emitted for resume attempts and resume success rate
